rationale: A single-deflator swap on the archive's strongest-alpha threshold gate is low-novelty and likely to yield a highly correlated portfolio, but the lt-vs-at contamination it addresses is real and the expression is internally consistent with the stated breakeven mechanism and negative sign.

The motive-plus-opportunity three-way gate is economically coherent and correctly signed, but it partly double-counts leverage because |pi/lt| already rises mechanically with the liability base, so any gain over the archived parents will be hard to attribute cleanly.

Gating the accrual flow on the stock of soft working capital relative to a depreciation-floored equity cushion is a substantively different construction from the archived level/trend gates, correctly signed, and the deflator floor is a thoughtful fix for negative-book-equity sign flips — though it edges toward the published net-operating-assets bloat anomaly and should be checked for overlap with it.

The stated "exact complement" claim is false — the archived asset-side leg already subtracts dp and this proposal subtracts it again, so the two halves sum to the net accrual minus depreciation rather than to the net measure, breaking the decomposition logic that is the proposal's entire justification.

A within-firm time-series rank of leverage is a genuinely different conditioning variable from the archive's cross-sectional levels and multi-year trends, removes firm and industry fixed effects as claimed, and is correctly signed — the main risk is that a 5-period annual TS_RANK is coarse and mechanically high for any firm merely growing its balance sheet.

Swapping RANK for IND_RANK on one leg of DeteriorationOnlyBitesWhenAlreadyLevered is a cosmetic variant whose gate will be highly rank-correlated with the original, so the test is unlikely to be diagnostic of anything beyond noise unless the proposal specifies how it will separate the industry-composition effect from the distress effect.
